AudioAssetStimulus.description:
A listening recording. Each listening section may carry its OWN track.

Per-part audio (Cambridge YLE ships one mp3 per part): consecutive listening
sections form one *track* while their `asset_id` stays the same; a section whose
`asset_id` differs from the previous audio section's starts a NEW track, and a
listening section with a non-audio stimulus (e.g. a matching pool) continues the
current one. The track's settings (`plays`, `locked`, `preview_asset_id`) come
from the section that starts it. Tracks play strictly in order (the runner never
lets a later part's track start before the current one has ended); the
furthest position per track (`asset_id`) is stored server-side
(`AudioTrackProgress`). One `asset_id` may only be used by consecutive sections
(the editor refuses A, B, A).

images.description: Optional context image asset_ids shown beside this stimulus.
images.title: Images

locked.description: When true the main track cannot be paused, seeked, or replayed once started (leaving/answering does not stop it); the preview clip stays free.
locked.title: Locked

plays.description: Replay limit for the main track. Default 1: Cambridge recordings already bake in the double play, so the online track is played once start-to-end.
plays.title: Plays

preview_asset_id.description: Optional sound-check / instructions clip (the recording's opening explanation), played BEFORE the main track and freely replayable.
preview_asset_id.title: Preview Asset Id

audio.description: The recording a LISTENING matching part plays (C1/C2 Listening Part 4: two parallel tasks, each with its own A-H pool, over one recording). It opens / continues a listening track exactly like an `audio_asset` stimulus: consecutive sections with the same `audio.asset_id` share ONE track (played once for both tasks). None = the part continues the current track.

each_option_once.description: True = every option fits at most ONE question (a gapped text: B2 Reading Part 6, C1 Part 7, C2 Part 6 - one option is a distractor); the runner greys out an option already used in this part. False = options are reusable (multiple matching: 'some options may be correct for more than one question'). Display hint only - grading compares each item's key.
